newsitem.title: USA: Muni yield curve unchanged over past week - Delphis.
newsitem.headline: Muni yield curve unchanged over past week - Delphis.

text.p: The municipal yield curve was unchanged in the week ended Thursday after steepening five basis points in the previous week, Delphis Hanover Corp. said Friday.
The spread between one-year and 30-year bonds in the triple-A category was unchanged at 185 basis points, after steepening five in each of the previous two weeks.
The Baa yield curve between one-year and thirty-year bonds was also unchanged, at 180 basis points, after steepening five the week before.

Average yields on one-year, Aaa-rated municipal bonds were flat at 3.75 percent, after falling five basis points in each of the previous two weeks. Baa-rated one-year bonds were also unchanged at 4.55 percent.
In the intermediate sector, yields on Aaa-rated 10-year bonds were unchanged for the second consecutive week at 4.90 percent, while Baa-rated ten-years held steady at 5.70 percent.
Long-term municipals mostly kept pace with the Treasury market over the week, after outperforming the week before.

The yield on the Treasury's 30-year bond fell just one basis point over the period to 6.98 percent. Thirty-year municipal yields, meanwhile, were unchanged for the third week in a row at 5.60 percent.
Yields were also unchanged on 30-year, Baa-rated bonds, holding at 6.35 percent.
Thirty-year, Aaa-rated munis yielded 80.2 percent of Treasury long bond at the close Thursday, compared to 80.1 percent the week before.
The credit spread between Aaa-rated and Baa-rated one-years was unchanged for the second consecutive week at 80 basis points. The 30-year spread was also unchanged again at 75 basis points.
To see Delphis Hanover's entire yield chart for the week, double click on nN30359024.
